work.abstract_text: For Zhan–Gupta–Hillery, Section 5, Conjecture 2 (2024, p. 10:11; arXiv:2306.17401v6, p. 11), we derive a strict-averaging counterexample from the complementary-layer Gram formula of Skotiniotis et al. (2018). Two different coefficient-square distributions and their whole averaging segment have the same Gram matrix and, for three sensors at theta = pi/4, the same error (14 - 4*sqrt(10))/27. We extend the earlier symmetric-probe calculation by proving weak convexity and the existence of a symmetric pure optimum without a symmetry assumption. This proves the companion Conjecture 1 and answers the source’s final question: one probe is optimal for both minimum-error and unambiguous discrimination at every detector angle. The reductions also apply to fixed unequal priors and diagonal impact patterns, without solving their general optimizers.

authors.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

work.title: Flat averages refute Zhan–Gupta–Hillery, Section 5, Conjecture 2 (2024, p. 10:11): an extension of Skotiniotis et al. (2018)
